fit.gap_handling_summary: The documents accurately present adjacent BigQuery, dbt, Python, batch-workflow and limited Docker experience rather than fabricating platform operations. Deployment ownership is particularly well bounded. However, the senior-level gaps in shared-platform architecture, scale, query optimisation, governance, access control and infrastructure are not meaningfully addressed, and the closest genuine orchestration evidence—dbt Cloud scheduling—is omitted. Unit testing supports engineering discipline, not ownership of platform-wide data quality or governance.

issues: Two pages are acceptable for six years of experience, but the second page is only 14.3% filled.
The MSc heading is at the bottom of page one while its dissertation begins page two.
The personal image-classification course project is correctly labelled but adds little to this platform-engineering application and contributes to the inefficient page break.
The profile is credible but presents an engineering transition rather than evidence of senior platform ownership.

keywords_missing_but_candidate_has: Google Cloud — supported as a platform label for the documented BigQuery and Vertex AI Workbench usage, not as infrastructure expertise
reasons: Single-column text extraction preserves headings, dates, bullets and words in a sensible reading order.
The CV contains several central stack terms, including BigQuery, dbt, Python, SQL, Docker and Git.
Google Cloud is demonstrated through named services but is not explicitly written as a platform keyword.
Many senior-platform and infrastructure terms are absent because the candidate's material does not establish those capabilities.
The current title and achievements remain predominantly data-science oriented; no platform-scale ownership or warehouse optimisation evidence is supplied.

issues: The Streamlit achievement is repeated in consecutive sentences: “and built a Streamlit application for planning and analysing sequential experiments. I built a Streamlit application for planning and analysing sequential experiments”.
It does not explain why a candidate moving toward production engineering is applying for a senior platform-ownership role.
The narrative concentrates on forecasting and churn rather than clearly mapping the closest genuine experience to reusable platform features.
BigQuery production SQL and dbt maintenance are repeated, and the two closing invitations to discuss a contribution are redundant.
Company tailoring is accurate but limited to the team remit and broad collaboration/ownership values.
strengths: Correct company, team and role throughout.
No stale references to currently working at Firth Energy Retail or still learning Python.
Quantified forecasting outcomes and testing coverage provide concrete evidence.
Explicitly credits the platform team with Cloud Run deployment rather than taking unsupported ownership.
Uses the advertised shared-framework focus and the company's collaboration and ownership values.
Professional English and an appropriate one-page length.

parsed.summary: The documents are factually disciplined, with useful quantified achievements and unusually clear boundaries around course work, Docker experience and deployment ownership. They present credible adjacent BigQuery, dbt and Python experience, but do not establish the architecture, operations, governance or scale expected of a senior data-platform owner. The strongest missed opportunity is the candidate's actual dbt Cloud scheduling experience. A duplicated Streamlit passage weakens the letter, while the nearly empty second CV page and split education entry make the PDF look insufficiently edited.
